The text contrasts the theme of inherent human evil with the theme of societal corruption. In William Golding's 'Lord of the Flies', the presentation suggests that savagery is an innate quality that emerges when social structures are removed, as seen in the boys' descent into chaos. Conversely, Jean-Jacques Rousseau’s philosophy presents the opposite view, arguing that humans are naturally good and free, and it is the constraints of society that introduce corruption. While both texts address the nature of humanity and its moral state, they differ fundamentally in their conclusions: Golding posits that evil is internal and inherent, whereas Rousseau posits that evil is external and imposed by social constructs.

The organ that pumps blood is the heart.
